references.text: The people asked Moses to speak to them instead of God, because they feared they would die if God spoke directly to them.
The Lord's glory appeared as a consuming fire on top of the mountain, which highlights the people's fear of the great fire.
Moses asks if anyone has ever heard God's voice speaking from the fire and survived, linking this to the people's fear of dying.
At Horeb, the people begged not to hear the Lord's voice or see the great fire anymore, so that they would not die.
The book of Hebrews refers to the terrifying experience at Sinai with fire and darkness, where the people pleaded that no more should be spoken to them.
